title: Model Catalog demo - PeakMed
summary: Quick walkthrough of Redwood's model catalog, benchmark results, and compatibility matrix. Customer interested in open models, quantization options, and running a short pilot for triage and summarization use cases. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot on Dedicated with a benchmark script; Redwood to share pricing and compatibility matrix plus security docs.
topics: Model selection for triage & summarization workloads
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment considerations
Security and compliance (KMS, audit logs, SSO)
action_items: Alex Chen - Send detailed pricing and model-compatibility matrix - due 2026-12-17
Priya Patel - Share benchmark scripts and sample prompts for triage use case - due 2026-12-14
Jamal Ortiz - Share PeakMed's data residency and KMS requirements - due 2026-12-13
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing + compatibility matrix
Redwood to provide benchmark script and sample dataset
Schedule pilot kick-off call week of 2026-12-20
PeakMed to confirm stakeholders and success criteria for pilot
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-10 15:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Patel, Ravi N., Sara Gomez, Tom R., Maya S., Jamal O.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya and Ravi on the solutions side. Quick round robin?
[00:12] Sara Gomez: Hi Sara, CTO here at PeakMed, we've got Tom and Maya and Jamal on the call. Big focus for us is triage workflows and extracting summaries from patient notes, latency and cost matter.
[00:25] Priya Patel: Great, thanks. Today's run through is the model catalog — selecting open models, looking at performance profiles, and the compatibility matrix for quantization and hardware. We'll also show console views in Optimize for batch config. A couple of quick clarifications: are you leaning hosted or dedicated for the pilot?
[00:42] Tom Reynolds: We're leaning Dedicated because of PII concerns and predictable throughput; also want to test on A100s we run on-prem.
[00:50] Priya Patel: Perfect; Dedicated gives you reserved pools and we can pin model variants. One note: some open models have different quantized kernels, so we show compat by hardware in the matrix.
[01:05] Maya Singh: Can you show a benchmark? sample latencies we should expect for 512 tokens and for short 64 token responses?
[01:12] Ravi Narayanan: Yep, we have a benchmark slide. So for 512 tokens on a single A100p3 variant with llama-like 13B q4 we typically see 180-220ms per token microbatches depending on KV cache hit rate, for 64 token responses it's more dominated by latency tail, around 60-90ms p95 for optimized kernels. Note: these are approximate, varies by prompt complexity.
[01:35] (note: audio glitch, 'p3' heard as 'pee three')
[01:40] Sara Gomez: Wait the numbers sound good but how do you measure the cost? is it per token or per GPU hour?
[01:47] Alex Chen: We provide both in the console: token-level breakdown + GPU-hours for Dedicated. Optimize suggests batching and quantization knobs that reduce unit cost. We'll send a cost sheet; for q4_0 quant you can see 20-30% cost improvement vs fp16 in many cases.
[02:05] Tom Reynolds: And compatibility matrix — will it tell us which quantization configs are supported on our on-prem A100 vs older V100?
[02:12] Priya Patel: Yes, the matrix maps model variants to kernel support per hardware profile and sequence length. For example, q4_0 and int8 paths are supported on A100 and Ampere clusters, but older V100 may not have optimized kernels for some int8 paths — fallback to slower fp16. We'll attach the matrix.
[02:34] Jamal Ortiz: Security — KMS support and audit logs? We need customer-managed keys and full audit trails for inference requests.
[02:42] Alex Chen: For Private/Dedicated we integrate with KMS/HSM; you can bring your own key and we log request-level metadata. We also support SSO/SAML and RBAC. We'll include SOC 2 + security deck.
[02:55] Maya Singh: Any gotchas with long context windows? We have some notes with 4k tokens.
[03:02] Ravi Narayanan: Context windows change kernel selection: with long sequences we prioritize memory-friendly kernels and KV cache reuse. For long prompt+response combos we recommend models optimized for long context (we show recommended variants in the catalog).
[03:20] (overlap) Alex Chen: Also note fallback policy — if a dedicated pool is full we'll route to compatible variants or to hosted as a fallback if you enable it.
[03:33] Tom Reynolds: About benchmarks — can we run a PeakMed-specific run? send scripts?
[03:38] Priya Patel: Yes, we'll send benchmark scripts and a conftest dataset. We can also run an optional Redwood-run benchmark and share the raw traces.
[03:48] (crosstalk) Sara Gomez: That would be helpful, we want to validate latency and hallucination rate on our prompt set.
[03:56] Priya Patel: On hallucination monitoring we have Redwood Optimize's quality monitoring tied to evals — you can register prompt sets and get regression alerts.
[04:07] Maya Singh: How about model updates and rollouts? We need pinning, canary, and automatic fallback.
[04:12] Ravi Narayanan: You can pin model versions per route, set canary percentages, and tie rollouts to perf/quality thresholds. If a canary fails, automatic rollback or fallback to pinned variant is supported.
[04:27] Jamal Ortiz: Any compliance constraints for data residency? we need EU residency for a subset of traffic.
[04:33] Alex Chen: We support region-level routing and private deployments in customer VPCs in specific cloud regions; we will capture residency requirements in the pilot scope.
[04:45] Tom Reynolds: Pricing: dedicated reserved vs burst — what's typical commit?
[04:50] Alex Chen: Reserved capacity is monthly/annual commits. We can model cost vs burst if you expect spiky traffic. I'll send a pricing scenario doc.
[04:58] (audio: 'pricing scenario' transcribed as 'rising scenario')
[05:03] Priya Patel: Quick demo of console — model catalog view (screen share): shows model family, size, recommended hardware, quantized variants, and benchmark profiles (latency/cost). You can filter by use case (summarization, triage) and get recommended knobs.
[05:25] Sara Gomez: That's helpful. Can we restrict particular models for production?
[05:29] Priya Patel: Yes, RBAC + route-level controls let you limit which teams can deploy certain models.
[05:35] Maya Singh: What about custom finetuned models? can we bring our own?
[05:39] Ravi Narayanan: You can bring your own model artifact, we support model-onboarding and packaging for serving. There's an onboarding checklist including compatibility testing on target hardware.
[05:50] Tom Reynolds: Pilot scope idea: 2-week Dedicated pilot, run triage benchmark (5k docs), compare q4_0 13B vs fp16 13B and 7B variants, measure latency, cost, and hallucination rate.
[06:02] Alex Chen: Sounds great. We'll map owners and timelines.
[06:06] Sara Gomez: Any dependencies on our infra? we'll need to share firewall rules for private deploy and KMS details.
[06:12] Priya Patel: Yes we'll need network access for the pilot; we'll share a checklist.
[06:18] (silence)
[06:20] Alex Chen: Recap: Redwood to send pricing, compatibility matrix, benchmark script, security docs. PeakMed to share KMS/residency requirements and pilot dataset. Schedule pilot kick-off week of 2026-12-20.
[06:36] Maya Singh: Great thanks everyone.
[06:38] Tom Reynolds: Thanks.
[06:40] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains some mis-heard words and occasional timestamps are approximate. Action items captured separately.
